title: An endomorphism is invertible iff its determinant is nonzero
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $V$ a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and $F:V\to V$ a $K$-linear endomorphism. Then $F$ is invertible (bijective, equivalently a unit of $\operatorname{End}_K(V)$) if and only if $\det(F\mid V)\neq0$ [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant].
